Public fields: question, answer. Internal: source, confidence, contested, notes_internal, and records with "publish": false. No row below is unverified.

facts.question: Who are The Luxury Liners?
facts.answer: The Luxury Liners are a power-pop band co-founded in 1997 by David Dewese and Chad Edgington, who took it to Nashville together. The name comes from the Gram Parsons song 'Luxury Liner'.

facts.question: Who founded The Luxury Liners?
facts.answer: David Dewese and his college friend Chad Edgington co-founded the band in 1997.
facts.contested: Older accounts (a 2005 band web page, AllMusic, Discogs) tell the start differently. The site follows the owner decision and does not repeat them (plan §4.3; LL-13).

facts.question: When and where did the band start?
facts.answer: David and Chad came up with the name over spring break 1997 in Texas, and moved the band to Nashville in May 1997. Nashville is the band’s home town.
facts.contested: Sources split between Texas and Nashville. Shown as: named in Texas, based in Nashville from May 1997; the town is never named (plan §4.3).

facts.question: Where does the name come from?
facts.answer: From the Gram Parsons song “Luxury Liner”.

facts.question: Is this Emmylou Harris’s Luxury Liner?
facts.answer: No. Emmylou Harris made an album called *Luxury Liner*, named after the same Gram Parsons song. The Luxury Liners are a band, and the band met Emmylou Harris in Nashville in the late 1990s.
facts.contested: The album's year is contested (1976 or 1977): no year is shown (plan §4.3).

facts.question: Is this Carter Tanton’s Luxury Liners?
facts.answer: No. Luxury Liners is also the recording name of the singer-songwriter Carter Tanton (*They’re Flowers*, 2013). That is a different act.

facts.question: Who is in the band?
facts.answer: The four forever members: David Dewese, Chad Edgington, Scott Carpenter and David “Larry” Wilstermann. All four play on the 2026 singles “Great Day” and “New Beginning”.

facts.question: Why is David Wilstermann called Larry?
facts.answer: Because the band already had a David when he joined on bass in December 2000.

facts.question: Who else has played in the band?
facts.answer: Jeff LaFrate (drums, 1997–98), Mark W. Winchester (bass, 1997–98), Kyle Edgington (drums, summer 1998) and Scott Jeffries (tambourine, one show, 1997) in the early days; later Gary Ishee (several shows in 2004–05, and guitar on *Nonetheless*), Doli Stepniewski (2006), and Grant Johnson and Jeremy Stephens (2007).

facts.question: When did Chad leave Nashville?
facts.answer: In March 2001, after his last show with the band. David carried the band on as a trio with Scott and Larry. Chad is one of the four forever members, he is in the band again today, and he plays on both 2026 singles.
facts.source: DECISIONS-2026-10-07.md LL-15, LL-9; daviddewese.com DECISIONS F4
facts.contested: March (photo title) versus April (2005 roster); LL-15 settles it as March 2001.

facts.question: Are they still a band?
facts.answer: Yes. The band never broke up. The four forever members reconnected during the pandemic and started making music again. They released “Great Day” and “New Beginning” in 2026.
facts.source: DECISIONS-2026-10-07.md LL-17 (verbatim sentences), LL-9; daviddewese.com DECISIONS F6

facts.question: Where is the band based?
facts.answer: Nashville is the band’s home town, the one city where all four forever members lived while pursuing the band. Today they are spread across Tennessee, Michigan and Texas.
facts.notes_internal: Never say which member lives where (LL-7, LL-19).

facts.question: What have they released?
facts.answer: *Sound As Ever* (album, May 2000), the *Believe* EP (March 2001), *Overbored* (album, May 2003), *Nonetheless* (album, October 2006), “Shake It Up (Live at the Texas Music Café)” (single, August 27, 2021), “Great Day” (single, February 13, 2026) and “New Beginning” (single, April 17, 2026). *Sound As Ever* came out on vinyl in 2026.
facts.notes_internal: Older releases are given to the month: their Spotify day is the first of the month, which reads as a placeholder.

facts.question: What is the newest release?
facts.answer: “New Beginning”, released on April 17, 2026. It pairs the song with “Great Day”.
facts.source: data/releases.json luxury-liners-2026-new-beginning; daviddewese.com DECISIONS F6, P6

facts.question: Which labels released their records?
facts.answer: Litterbug Records released *Overbored*, *Nonetheless* and the 2026 singles, and released *Sound As Ever* with Echomusic. Echomusic released the *Believe* EP. Texas Music Café released the 2021 live single.

facts.question: Has their music been on TV?
facts.answer: Yes. “Dreaming” was used in *One Tree Hill* (season 1, episode 15, “Suddenly Everything Has Changed”, The WB, February 24, 2004), and “Sunshine” became the theme of FOX Sports’ *US Youth Soccer Show*.

facts.question: Who produced the records?
facts.answer: Mike Poole produced most of *Sound As Ever*, and Mark Montgomery produced two of its tracks. Mark Montgomery produced the *Believe* EP with the band. Doug Nightwine recorded *Overbored* and Chris Henning mixed it, and Chris Henning mixed and mastered *Nonetheless*.

facts.question: Who wrote the songs?
facts.answer: Chad and David wrote most of *Sound As Ever* and both 2026 singles. David wrote *Nonetheless* and wrote or co-wrote nearly all of *Overbored*, and David Wilstermann wrote “Restless”. “Believe” on the *Believe* EP is a cover of Cher’s song; “Shake It Up” is the band’s own.
facts.source: DECISIONS-2026-10-07.md LL-14 (Nonetheless, Great Day, New Beginning; Discogs credits for Sound As Ever and Overbored stand); daviddewese.com DECISIONS P27; data/releases.json songwriting

facts.question: What does “Sound As Ever” mean?
facts.answer: It was Gram Parsons’s sign-off, “Sound as ever”. The band named its first album after it.

facts.question: Were they in Billboard?
facts.answer: Yes. The band was featured in *Billboard* in 1998.
facts.contested: Title and issue unknown until the clipping is found; none is shown (plan §4.3).

facts.question: Did they play SXSW?
facts.answer: Yes. The band played the SESAC Showcase at SXSW 2001.

facts.question: Is “Shake It Up” a cover?
facts.answer: No. It is a Luxury Liners original, first released on the *Believe* EP in 2001. The 2021 single is a live version, recorded live in Waco, Texas, in autumn 1998.

facts.question: How is the band connected to The Foxymorons?
facts.answer: David Dewese co-founded both bands; he started The Foxymorons with Jerry James. Songs moved between them: both bands recorded David’s “The Duke Of Gloucester”, and Mike Poole produced both bands’ first albums.
facts.source: daviddewese.com DECISIONS F5; DECISIONS-2026-10-07.md LL-14; research/01 §8

facts.question: Who made the cover art?
facts.answer: Mark Montgomery designed *Sound As Ever* and made the *Believe* EP cover; Jim Horan restored the *Sound As Ever* art for the 2026 vinyl. David made the covers of *Overbored*, “Shake It Up (Live)” (from a Mark Montgomery photo), “Great Day” and “New Beginning”.
facts.notes_internal: The Nonetheless credit (paintings: Scott Carpenter; design: David) is single-source and outside LL-23: held until David confirms.

facts.question: Where can I listen?
facts.answer: On Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube and the other streaming services, and on Bandcamp. The Listen page has the links.
facts.notes_internal: LL-27: no downloads; LL-36: Bandcamp is David's account (daviddewese.bandcamp.com), linked as the band's Bandcamp.

facts.question: How do I contact the band?
facts.answer: Use the form on the Contact page.
facts.notes_internal: The address the form sends to is never printed (LL-31).

facts.question: What is “Texas Pop”?
facts.answer: The band’s own name for its music, used on its website in the 2000s.
facts.source: research/03 §4.3 (the 2005 history intro, which also carries the talent-show story)
facts.notes_internal: Held: the only read source for the phrase is the 2005 history intro, whose story LL-13 removes entirely; a poster with the phrase is unread. Publish once another source is confirmed.

facts.question: Is Sound As Ever on vinyl?
facts.answer: Yes. It came out on vinyl in 2026, with the original art restored by Jim Horan.
facts.notes_internal: Label, edition size and remastering credit are single-source (Discogs 37658859); they go on the release page with attribution, not here.

dating_note.heading: How dates are given
dating_note.text: Release dates are the dates the streaming services list; for the older records the site gives the month. Where only a season or a range is known, the site says so. Where accounts differ, the band’s own answer stands.
